definitions.E1:
## Construction Management — Bachelor of Technology

This is a **degree-completion program** that develops management, technical, and interpersonal skills for construction projects.

- **School:** School of Construction and the Environment  
- **Credential:** Bachelor of Technology / Bachelor’s Degree  
- **Location:** Burnaby  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **Study options:** Full-time and part-time  
- **Status:** Active  

### Curriculum areas

The program includes:

- **Construction Controls and Techniques:**  
  **CMGT 7160** — Statistics for Construction Management; **CMGT 7190** — Construction Planning and Controls; **CMGT 7211** — Heavy Equipment in Construction; **CMGT 7400** — Project Planning for Quality & Risk Management

- **Organization Management:**  
  **BUSA 7250** — Management Skills and Applications; **CMGT 7330** — Finance for Construction Managers; **CMGT 7420** — Construction Law; **CMGT 8435** — Construction Enterprise Management

- **Stakeholder Engagement:**  
  **CMGT 7535** — Leadership and Interpersonal Skills; **CMGT 7660** — Environmental Considerations in Construction; **CMGT 8602** — Engagement of Project Stakeholders

- **Management electives:** Complete **at least 4 credits from the approved management-elective pool**. Options include **CMGT 7125** — Construction Schedule and Delay Analysis; **CMGT 7220** — Health and Safety in Construction; **CMGT 7605** — Industrial Relations; **CMGT 8040** — Building – Civil Services; **CMGT 8050** — Budgeting/Conceptual Estimating; and **CMGT 8060** — Risk Management in Design & Construction of Buildings. Other approved options include courses in engineering technology, project management, finance, marketing, human resources, and leadership.

- **Liberal Studies:** The standard component totals **12 credits**, including **LIBS 7001** — Critical Reading and Writing and **LIBS 7002** — Applied Ethics. Part-time students may replace **LIBS 7013** — Race, Class and Gender: Intersections with one additional 3-credit approved Liberal Studies elective.

- **Professional Standards:**  
  **CMGT 7810** — Advanced Industry Communication; **CMGT 8211** — Industry Collaborations; and **CMGT 8700** — Industry Based Project Proposal. Students then choose **one** final-project option: **CMGT 8800** — Industry Based Project or **CMGT 8810** — Industry Based Project. The final-project options require department approval.

### Entry pathways

Admission includes an approved departmental pre-entry assessment and **English Studies 12 at 73% or equivalent**, plus **exactly one** of four entry pathways involving a related or unrelated credential, construction experience, a bridging credential, or an approved Red Seal trade. The detailed requirements differ by pathway. A master’s degree alone is not sufficient for admission.

### Additional completion requirements

The program requires at least **two years of related work experience** for capstone and graduation work-experience eligibility; qualifying admission experience counts toward this total. **CMGT 8700** requires completion of the required program coursework before the student’s chosen final-project course, two years of related work experience, an industry topic, and an industry sponsor.

For full program details, see the [Construction Management Bachelor of Technology program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/construction-management-bachelor-of-technology-full-time-part-time-8800btech/).
definitions.E3:
## Construction Management — Bachelor of Technology

This is an active, in-person degree-completion program offered full-time or part-time at the Burnaby campus by the School of Construction and the Environment.

### Admission requirements

All applicants must meet these common requirements:

- Complete an approved departmental pre-entry assessment before applying.
- Have **English Studies 12 with at least 73%**, or an equivalent.
- Meet **exactly one** of the following entry pathways:

**Pathway A — Related post-secondary credential**
- A construction-related diploma or degree from a recognized institution with at least **67% GPA**.
- At least **one year of construction-industry work experience**.

**Pathway B — Unrelated post-secondary credential plus bridging credential**
- An unrelated diploma or degree from a recognized institution with at least **67% GPA**.
- A **BCIT Construction Operations Associate Certificate** with at least **67% GPA**.
- At least **one year of construction-industry work experience**.

**Pathway C — Extensive construction-management experience**
- An unrelated diploma or degree from a recognized institution with at least **67% GPA**.
- At least **eight years of North American construction-management experience** in mid- or senior-level roles.

**Pathway D — Red Seal trade**
- An approved Red Seal trade: cabinetmaker, carpenter, electrician, industrial mechanic/millwright, metal fabricator, plumber, refrigeration and air-conditioning mechanic, or welder Level A.
- One accepted mathematics option with at least **60%**: Pre-Calculus 11, Foundations Math 11, Workplace Math 11, **BLDT 1011**, or an accepted B.C./Yukon equivalent.
- A Construction Operations Associate Certificate with at least **67% GPA**.
- At least **one year of construction-industry experience**, in addition to apprenticeship hours.

### Additional credential requirement

For specified international post-secondary credentials from outside Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, and New Zealand, the record requires an accepted comprehensive credential evaluation, including course-by-course evaluation and GPA calculation. An accepted service may include an ICES comprehensive evaluation.

A **master’s degree alone is not sufficient** for admission.

For international applicants, the program is recorded as available, but the study-permit status is listed as **not published** in the available data. Confirmation with the institution is recommended.

[Program details and application information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/construction-management-bachelor-of-technology-full-time-part-time-8800btech/)

For more information, see BCIT Admissions: https://www.bcit.ca/admission/.
